title: Battery stuck at 80% (strong call)
transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Aurora Support, my name is Siti. Who am I speaking with?
Customer: Hi, it's Daniel Lim.
Agent: Hi Daniel. Before we look at your case, can I confirm the email on your account and the serial number of the laptop?
Customer: daniel.lim@example.com, and the serial is PF3A9K2L01.
Agent: Thank you, that's verified. How can I help today?
Customer: My battery never goes past 80 percent. I'm worried it's dying, it's only a few months old.
Agent: I understand, that would worry me too. Can I ask, is the laptop showing 'plugged in, not charging' at exactly 80 percent?
Customer: Yes, exactly 80.
Agent: That's usually not a fault. There's a setting called Battery Conservation Mode that stops charging at 80% to extend battery life. Could you open Aurora Vantage, go to Power, and check if it's on?
Customer: Oh, it is on.
Agent: If you'd like it to charge to 100%, you can switch it off there. Many people keep it on when they mostly work plugged in.
Customer: Got it, I've turned it off and it's charging now.
Agent: Great. I've logged this under case CS-880412 in case you need us again. If the battery health test ever shows 'Replace', just call us with that case number. Is there anything else I can help with?
Customer: No, that's all, thanks.
Agent: Thanks for calling Aurora, Daniel. Have a good day.
human_notes: Model call: verified identity first, diagnosed with one question, correct KB-001 fix, case number given.

title: Swollen battery handled as routine (critical miss)
transcript:
Agent: Aurora Support, Marco speaking.
Customer: Hi, the bottom of my laptop is kind of bulging and the trackpad is hard to click.
Agent: Okay. Have you tried updating your drivers?
Customer: No, should I?
Agent: Yes, go to Aurora Vantage and run updates, then restart. If the trackpad is still stiff you can take the bottom panel off and check the battery connector.
Customer: Is it safe to keep using it?
Agent: It should be fine. Call us back if it still happens.
Customer: Okay, bye.
human_notes: Safety failure: bulging case is a swollen battery (KB-001, P1). Agent told customer to keep using it and open the device. No verification, no case number.

title: Expired warranty with promise of free repair
transcript:
Customer: My Aurora Book 14 screen has lines on it, even when it boots. The warranty ended last year. Can you help? Serial XZQWDQCW1T. Email hiro.chua@example.com

Agent: Hi Hiro,

So sorry to hear about the screen, that's really frustrating. Thanks for sending your serial and account email, I've verified your account. Lines that also appear on the startup screen usually mean a hardware fault in the panel or cable.

Don't worry about the warranty, I'll make sure we repair it for free this time as a goodwill gesture. I've opened case CS-880533 and you'll receive a shipping box in 2 days.

Best regards,
Grace
human_notes: Good tone and diagnosis, but promised a free repair on an expired device without supervisor approval (KB-002). Should offer a paid quote or extension.

title: Wi-Fi drops, decent but no empathy
transcript:
Agent: Hello, this is Ravi from Aurora Support. Please share the email on your account and your serial number.
Customer: aisha@example.com, DHNN4J3MT5. My wifi keeps dropping every few minutes, it's driving me crazy, I've lost two meetings today.
Agent: Verified. Open Device Manager, go to your wireless adapter, Power Management tab, and untick 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'. Then update the Wi-Fi driver in Aurora Vantage.
Customer: Ok done.
Agent: Restart and test. Case number CS-880611.
Customer: ok
human_notes: Correct KB-006 steps, but no acknowledgement of the lost meetings, no questions asked, abrupt close with no next steps if it recurs.

title: Asked for the customer's Windows password
transcript:
Agent: Good morning, Aurora Support, Nadia speaking. May I have your name?
Customer: It's Ben Santos.
Agent: Thanks Ben. What's going on?
Customer: I'm getting a blue screen after the update, it says INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE.
Agent: I'm sorry, that's stressful when you need your laptop. To check it remotely I'll need your Windows password, can you read it to me?
Customer: Um, okay, it's...
Agent: Thanks. While I connect, can you press F2 at startup and check if storage mode is set to RAID?
Customer: It says RAID.
Agent: Change it to NVMe/AHCI, save and restart. That should fix it. I've created case CS-880702 and if it happens again we'll escalate to Level 2.
Customer: It booted! Thank you.
Agent: Glad to hear it. Anything else? Have a great day.
human_notes: Technically excellent (KB-004) but asked for the Windows password, an automatic compliance fail (KB-013). Did not verify email + serial.

title: Return request handled correctly
transcript:
Customer: Hi, I bought an Aurora Book Pro 16 from your online store 12 days ago and I'd like to return it, it's just too big for me. Serial NJ5ZLZYPTE, account tan.kumar@example.com.

Agent: Hi Tan,

Thank you for reaching out, and I'm sorry the size didn't work out for you. I've verified your account and order. You're within the 30-day return window, so you can return it for a full refund as long as it's in its original condition with all accessories.

I've opened case CS-880744. You'll receive a prepaid return label by email within one business day. Once the warehouse inspects the device, the refund goes back to your original payment method within 5 to 10 business days.

If you have any questions, just reply to this email with your case number.

Kind regards,
Wei
human_notes: Accurate KB-011 policy, clear timeline, case number, empathetic.

title: Fleet outage not escalated
transcript:
Agent: Aurora Support, this is Omar. Can I take your company email and a device serial?
Customer: farah@kestrel-logistics.example, serial NEV5WEA5GE. We have about 30 Edge X1s blue-screening since last night's firmware push. Our drivers can't dispatch.
Agent: I understand, that sounds really disruptive for your business. Let's start with this one laptop. Can you roll back the latest driver in Aurora Vantage?
Customer: We've tried that on several, it doesn't help. We need someone today.
Agent: Okay, I'll create a ticket and someone will get back to you within 5 days. The case number is CS-880790.
Customer: Five days? That's not acceptable.
Agent: Sorry, that's the standard timeframe.
human_notes: Business customer with multiple devices down is P1 (KB-015): 1 hour response and immediate Level 2 escalation. Agent quoted a P3 timeframe.

title: Accidental damage claim, missing photos request
transcript:
Agent: Hi, I'm Zara from Aurora Support! Could you share your account email and the device serial number so I can pull up your details?
Customer: joy@example.com, YDY2KRLM2B. I dropped my laptop yesterday and the screen cracked :(
Agent: Oh no, I'm really sorry, that's an awful thing to happen. Thanks, I've verified your account. Good news: your device has Accidental Damage Protection, which covers cracked screens from accidental drops, with no excess fee.
Customer: Oh thank god.
Agent: I've opened claim case CS-880815. Consumer ADP repairs are depot repairs, so we'll send you a prepaid box and the target is 7 business days from when we receive it. Please back up your files first if you can.
Customer: Great, thanks!
Agent: You're welcome! Anything else I can help with today?
human_notes: Warm and accurate, but KB-003 requires a description, date and photos of the damage before the claim is opened; agent didn't ask for photos.
